A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SEMMA and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H. Content can be reliably matched despite changes in pagination and placement.

before.justification: v1 reports original link-prediction experiments across 54 evaluation KGs, component ablations, leakage analyses, and harder unseen-relation tests in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports threshold-sensitivity observations and tuning work in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The dual structural/textual NBFNet pipeline, embedding construction, fusion, training objective, and hybrid switch remain unchanged. The example triples explicitly mentioned in v2 Section 4.1 were already included in v1’s prompt in Figure 5.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same three pretraining KGs, 54 evaluation KGs, 22-KG leakage-filtered subset, and harder FBNELL/Metafam scenarios. Calibration and complex-query answering are proposed only as future work.

E2.justification: ULTRA remains the comparator in the aggregate, leakage-filtered, harder-setting, and dataset-level comparisons. The ablation alternatives also remain unchanged; newly discussed BLP, StatiK, and SimKGC are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Table 9 changes reported training steps from 200,000 to 800,000 and negatives from 128 to 512. These fourfold revisions substantially change the stated training budget and negative-sampling setting, although the PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun or earlier reporting was corrected.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds a sensitivity-analysis paragraph reporting a threshold search over {0.6, 0.7, 0.79, 0.8} and qualitative inspection of generated edges on a dataset subset. This extends v1’s conceptual threshold discussion, but supplies no threshold-wise scores or new analysis figure.

E5.justification: Both versions report five runs, standard deviations, and the same Mann–Whitney U tests. Section 5.3 retains p-values of 0.0040 for average MRR and 0.0278 for average Hits@10.

E6.justification: All tabulated performance values remain unchanged, including Table 1’s total MRR of 0.365 for ULTRA and 0.374 for SEMMA. The limited addition is Appendix E’s explicit qualitative finding of observed threshold sensitivity; no threshold-wise numerical outcomes are provided.

T1.justification: Section 2 corrects the partially inductive target entity set from E_T minus E_O to E_TEST minus E_TRAIN, distinguishing unseen-at-training entities from unobserved entities. The method equations and Appendix F’s relation-disjointness condition remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution bullets retain the same claims about combining textual and structural signals, performance across 54 KGs, advantages after leakage filtering, and harder unseen-relation generalization. Added future directions do not expand the claimed demonstrated contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly qualifies LLM enrichment as beneficial but not necessarily optimal across contexts, discusses dynamic thresholding, and adds calibration and complex-query answering as future extensions. Existing explanations of dataset-dependent performance and leakage limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds a public SEMMA repository link in the introduction, whereas v1 points to supplementary code and a checkpoint. It also discloses the threshold-search grid and revises two Table 9 hyperparameters; the remaining implementation, hardware, runtime, and prompting details are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds BLP, StatiK, and SimKGC as evidence for transferable textual representations. The conclusion adds references on calibration and complex-query reasoning. These are localized expansions; the positioning relative to ULTRA, PROLINK, and Appendix H’s parallel works remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized rewrites to the introduction, preliminaries, prompting explanation, conclusion, and acknowledgments, and formats the research questions separately. Section 5.3 replaces the ambiguous '9 points' and '7 points' wording with qualitative wording while retaining the underlying table values.

P2.justification: All eight figures and twelve tables are retained, with unchanged figure artwork. Table 3 changes column placement, Table 10 moves from sharing a page with Table 9 to a separate page, and caption emphasis, spacing, and page breaks are adjusted.

improvement.justification: The corrected entity-set expression, public code link, threshold-search disclosure, and expanded prior-work context modestly improve precision and reproducibility information. Empirical scores remain unchanged, and the unexplained Table 9 revisions leave the provenance of the reported training settings unclear, limiting the overall gain.
